item.text:
The design can satisfy the requested outcome with local corrections. The main gaps are permissions recovery, claimed layouts retaining tools in Chats, and the window-wide consequences of disabling Tauri’s drop handler.

The coverage map includes the user’s requirements, the selected design’s behavioral commitments, and its delivery gates. “Partial” means a location exists but its implementation or acceptance criterion needs correction.

| Explicit requirement | Plan location | Acceptance criterion and coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Simplify the empty conversation while retaining OpenPane’s appearance | 00 Requested outcome; 01; 04 Integration gate | Empty state contains the specified composer controls and shell footer; compare requested screenshots in dark and light appearance. Covered, subject to findings below. |
| Leave both left navigation panes unchanged in markup and CSS | 00 Scope; 01 Exclusions; 04 | Screenshot comparison plus scoped markup/CSS diff. **Partial:** DoD explicitly checks CSS selectors but should also inspect navigation markup. |
| Limit changes to this screen and components it uses | 00 Scope and non-goals; 01 Empty workspace | Shared effort control changes are included; picker behavior, iOS, pairing, attestation, and a new settings page remain outside scope. Covered. |
| Use a direct cutover without flags or compatibility shims | 00 Application context | Review final diff for a single implementation without transitional paths. Covered. |
| Hide the visible header while retaining its accessibility and test hooks | 01 Header; Acceptance 2–3 | Heading remains discoverable by accessible name; header is visually hidden; `.scope-label` remains readable through `textContent`. Covered. |
| Remove the empty invitation text, disabled effort chip, and composer disclosure | 01 Changes; Acceptance 2 | Elements are absent or hidden as specified; agent-routing assertions expect only the two remaining chips. Covered. |
| Show only the caret when typing; remove the composer focus highlight | 01 CSS; Acceptance 4 | Focused composer has `box-shadow: none`; textarea has no focus outline; button focus indicators remain. Covered. |
| Remove the resize grip and grow the textarea until a cap, then scroll | 01 Textarea and CSS; Acceptance 4–5 | `resize: none`; height grows, caps, and scrolls. **Partial:** hidden-view updates and width changes are unhandled; ten lines do not reliably exceed `40vh`. See finding 7. |
| Center a genuinely empty conversation; place the composer at the bottom after content appears | 01 Empty predicate; Acceptance 1, 8 | Center within the specified tolerance; first message removes `data-empty`. **Partial:** predicate omits other rendered content. See finding 8. |
| Preserve sending, stopping, draft behavior, and harness/model picker behavior | 00 Non-goals; 01 Textarea and Send; 03 Drop states | Accessible “Send” still submits; Stop and picker behavior remain; saved draft survives attachment rejection. **Partial:** add explicit regression checks for these retained behaviors. |
| Move disclosure to the shell footer only for Chats with an active conversation | 01 BrowserApplication; Acceptance 7 | Exact Codex disclosure appears in Chats; other views and no-conversation state retain `buildLabel`; extension-only tests retain their forbidden-text assertions. Covered. |
| Hide unsupported permissions while preserving supported-provider refresh and both revoke paths | 02 Permissions; Acceptance 1–2 | Codex has no Permissions region; Crew exposes refresh and both revoke flows. **Partial:** first-read failure recovery and refresh ownership remain unresolved. See finding 1. |
| Move custom tools off the conversation screen and into Extensions | 00 Success 5; 02 Custom tools; Acceptance 3–4 | No module buttons in Chats; modules act from Extensions. **Conflicting:** claimed layouts retain full modules in Chats. See finding 2. |
| Render nothing for empty module sets | 00 Success 5; 02 CustomizationModules | No empty fieldsets, wrappers, or resulting spacing. **Partial:** `status`/`all` wrapper behavior is not specified adequately. See finding 3. |
| Keep customization loading/failure notices and recovery available | 02 Surfaces; Acceptance 5; alert tests | Existing loading text and exact failure alert remain in the conversation column; Restore default view remains usable. Covered, but include notices in empty-state verification. |
| Identify the conversation targeted by Extensions tools and preserve action behavior | 02 BrowserApplication and ExtensionsList; Acceptance 4 | Display catalog label or conversation ID fallback; action updates the named conversation; verify draft and scope after returning to Chats. **Partial:** section visibility needs unified eligibility. See finding 2. |
| Preserve claimed-layout behavior | 02 `surface="all"`; Acceptance 6 | Existing content-layout tests are expected unchanged. **Conflicting:** preserving module placement violates tools relocation. Resolve explicitly in finding 2. |
| Provide panel-wide PNG/JPEG drop and an accessible “+” picker | 03 Goal and Changes; Acceptance 1–3 | Drop onto transcript and composer attaches; Tab/Enter opens picker; accessible names and `Image file` remain. Covered for browser simulation; native completion remains conditional. |
| Preserve one-image, type, size, and host-authority constraints | 03 `image-intake.ts` | Exactly one PNG/JPEG, filename fallback only for empty MIME type, size at most `IMAGE_MAX_BYTES`; host validates content. Covered. |
| Reject invalid or blocked attachment attempts with an explanation and preserve draft/existing image | 00 Success 4; 03 Validation and Drop states | Test all rejection reasons and assert unchanged draft/image. **Partial:** current tests do not assert preservation, and rejected real-drop delivery is unproven. See findings 5–6. |
| Ignore text drags and prevent file-drop navigation | 03 Drop zone; Acceptance 2; 04 WP4 | Text drags remain untouched; file drops inside and outside the panel cannot navigate. **Missing implementation outside the panel.** See finding 4. |
| Keep compact attachment status, Retry, Remove, replacement, and image-only Send | 03 Chip placement and Drop states | Preserve labels/statuses and existing picker tests; verify Retry, Remove, replacement, and image-only Send. Covered; add unchanged-image rejection assertions. |
| Disable native drag handling without introducing native-path drop support | 03 Tauri config; Exclusions; 04 WP4 | Confirm no existing native-event consumer; pass Finder drop in desktop development. **Conflicting completion rule:** fallback-only success is allowed despite required drop behavior. See finding 9. |
| Verify browser, customization, provider, and host regressions | 01–03 Test sections; 04 Work packages and Integration gate | Run listed targeted tests and `npm run verify`; update only assertions affected by intended behavior. Covered, with sequencing correction in finding 1. |
| Verify appearance, narrow layout, and delivery hygiene | 04 Integration gate and DoD | Capture empty/image/Crew states; check light appearance, 520px overflow, unchanged navigation; exclude generated artifacts. Covered. |
| Keep greeting, clipboard paste, multiple images, native-path fallback, and effort settings deferred | 00 Non-goals; 03 Exclusions; 04 Deferred | None appears in the implementation. Covered, except native fallback must not waive required drop acceptance. |

Material findings:

1. **Blocking — Permissions visibility also controls recovery lifecycle.**  
   **Location:** 02 Permissions; 01 empty predicate; 04 WP1–WP2.  
   **Evidence:** `ConversationPermissions` owns the window-focus refresh listener. The proposed gate unmounts it for `loading`/`stale` with `listing: null`. The plan explicitly leaves first-read failure handling undecided. The packet does not establish another recovery owner. WP1 also needs `permissionsShown`, which WP2 introduces later.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** A first-read failure can hide both the explanation and Refresh control, while removing the shown focus-refresh mechanism. An agent may use reason-string matching or produce a WP1 intermediate state that cannot pass its checks.  
   **Correction:** Resolve this before implementation. Keep refresh lifecycle independent of card visibility, and represent initial/unread versus failed-first-read through explicit state rather than reason text. Failed reads must expose a retry path. Introduce the visibility helper before, or together with, its first caller.  
   **Acceptance:** Unsupported Codex remains quiet; a failed first supported-provider read exposes an explanation and retry; focus refresh remains available before a successful listing; every work package passes its stated checks.

2. **Blocking — Claimed layouts contradict tools relocation, and tool-section eligibility is split.**  
   **Location:** 02 `surface="all"`, BrowserApplication routing, ExtensionsList.  
   **Evidence:** 00 requires custom modules to leave the conversation screen. 02 instead passes full modules to claimed layouts and suppresses their Extensions copy. Separately, `hasTools` checks only namespace readiness and module count, whereas `tools` additionally requires an active conversation and a non-claimed layout.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** Tools remain in Chats for claimed layouts. Extensions can render an empty “Conversation tools” section when its node is suppressed but `hasTools` is true.  
   **Correction:** Apply relocation consistently to claimed layouts: pass status notices through the existing `modules` slot and render ready tools in Extensions. No signature change is needed. Derive section visibility and its nodes from one eligibility calculation, including active-conversation and action availability. Resolve slot selection before choosing its module nodes. Update claimed-layout fixtures deliberately rather than promising unchanged module-placement assertions.  
   **Acceptance:** A claimed-layout fixture has no tool buttons in Chats and working tools in Extensions. No tools section appears without an eligible conversation. Tests reopen Extensions before each subsequent tool interaction after returning to Chats.

3. **Blocking — Empty fieldsets can become empty padded wrappers.**  
   **Location:** 02 `CustomizationModules` surfaces.  
   **Evidence:** The existing outer `.customization-panel` has `padding: 8px 0`. The plan preserves its `<aside>` for `status`, while only explicitly making the inner `ConversationModules` return null for empty arrays.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** Ready namespaces with no status content leave empty asides and spacing on the supposedly composer-only canvas. `all` can have the same problem.  
   **Correction:** Specify top-level null returns: `status` renders nothing for ready namespaces; `tools` renders nothing without usable modules; `all` renders nothing when neither notices nor usable modules exist. Preserve namespace attributes on wrappers that actually render content.  
   **Acceptance:** Empty ready namespaces produce no customization wrappers or fieldsets and add no layout height.

4. **Blocking — Outside-panel navigation prevention has no owner.**  
   **Location:** 03 Drop zone and Tauri config; 04 WP4.  
   **Evidence:** Disabling `dragDropEnabled` affects the window. The proposed HTML handlers exist only on `.conversation-panel`, yet acceptance requires dropping on the sidebar not to navigate.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** Panel drops work, but drops elsewhere retain browser/webview default behavior.  
   **Correction:** Add a shell/document-level file-drag guard that prevents default navigation without attaching files. Keep attachment handling on the panel, leave text drags alone, and clean up listeners. This requires no navigation markup or CSS changes.  
   **Acceptance:** Real file drops on the sidebar, rail, and shell background neither navigate nor attach; panel drops still attach.

5. **Improvement — Rejected-drop feedback depends on an unverified event sequence.**  
   **Location:** 03 Drop zone, Drop states, synthetic browser tests.  
   **Evidence gap:** The plan sets `dropEffect = 'none'` for rejected drags, then relies on `onDrop` to publish the rejection alert. Manually dispatched events do not establish that a real rejected drag will deliver that drop event.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** Synthetic GIF/multiple-file tests pass, while a real drag clears or retains only transient feedback and never produces the promised alert.  
   **Correction:** Choose rejection handling that guarantees the specified feedback under real dragging. If a post-drop alert is required, use an event policy that permits delivery and reject during intake. Always validate the actual dropped files and current blocked state at drop time.  
   **Acceptance:** Exercise an actual invalid drag, verify the resulting explanation, and confirm drag feedback clears after cancellation or completion.

6. **Improvement — The shared attachment boundary does not enforce its own blocked state.**  
   **Location:** 03 `attach`, block reason, picker/drop callers.  
   **Evidence:** Proposed `attach(files)` validates files but never checks `blocked`. It awaits `arrayBuffer()` before calling `selectImage`; the packet supplies no store-level concurrency guarantee for overlapping reads or replacements.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** Picker and drop callers can enforce different rules. Multiple intake operations can begin before the upload status changes. Whether the store safely rejects them is unknown.  
   **Correction:** Enforce current attachment eligibility in the shared intake boundary. Verify the store’s concurrency contract; add a per-store pending-intake guard only if that contract does not already provide protection. Keep rejection alerts outside any `image || acceptsImages` rendering gate so unsupported-agent drops can explain themselves.  
   **Acceptance:** Overlapping attempts and a picker completed after eligibility changes cannot replace or clear an existing image improperly. Rejections preserve both draft text and the prior attachment.

7. **Blocking — Text-only auto-grow misses hidden-view and width changes.**  
   **Location:** 01 Textarea; 02 module-action tests.  
   **Evidence:** Auto-grow runs only when `editor.text` changes. BrowserApplication keeps Chats mounted under a hidden `.shell-view` while Extensions is selected. Module actions can update the draft there.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** Measurement can run without a visible layout, then fail to rerun on returning to Chats. Resizing can also change wrapping without changing text. A multiline draft can therefore remain at the wrong height.  
   **Correction:** Recalculate when the textarea becomes measurable and when its available width changes, as well as on text changes. Keep the mechanism local to sizing. Replace “ten lines reaches the cap” with content whose measured height exceeds the computed cap.  
   **Acceptance:** Update a multiline draft from Extensions, return to Chats, and verify correct height. Also verify width changes, shrinking after clearing, and scrolling beyond the cap.

8. **Improvement — The empty predicate does not describe all visible content.**  
   **Location:** 01 Empty predicate.  
   **Evidence:** It covers messages, decisions, continuation, observation, availability, and permissions, but omits customization notices/conflicts, activity contributions, and `CommandRecovery`. `CommandActivity` and `FileActivity` returning null when empty does not establish that zero messages implies empty activity.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** Loading, error, conflict, or recovery content can receive empty-canvas centering and transcript padding removal.  
   **Correction:** Define `empty` as eligibility for the special centered layout. Account for known notice/activity/recovery states; where absence cannot be established from available state, keep the normal layout. Do not infer DOM emptiness from ReactNode truthiness.  
   **Acceptance:** Add zero-message cases with customization failure, layout conflict, activity, and retained command recovery. Their controls remain visible and usable in the normal layout.

9. **Blocking — The completion rule waives a required outcome.**  
   **Location:** 00 Risks; 03 Acceptance 2; 04 Definition of done.  
   **Evidence:** Finder-to-panel attachment is required, but DoD permits reporting picker success and filing a native-drop follow-up when Finder dropping fails. The packet expressly identifies WKWebView delivery as an assumption.  
   **Implementing-agent failure mode:** The change is declared complete after failing its primary new attachment interaction.  
   **Correction:** Make real macOS Finder dropping a required completion gate. If it fails, record the unmet requirement and supporting evidence; the picker is useful recovery, but does not satisfy drag-and-drop acceptance. Consider native-path handling only if that failure establishes the selected approach cannot meet the requirement.  
   **Acceptance:** Report an observed successful Finder-to-transcript attachment and successful outside-panel navigation prevention before marking the work complete.
